_about: Mobile anti-aircraft gun (Track M2U, mission 2, 2026-10-11). ALEX'S: the second mission profile, 'Clear mobile Aa units and their escorts to enable a bombing run of a military complex' (decision suppress-mission; the mission idea is Alex's, everything below is PROPOSED by Track M2U). A light AA gun on a tracked or half-tracked chassis: a GROUND unit that drives (the tank's movement system with its own numbers: the same envelope, steered by pivot, the ground rule of data/sim/ground.json applying to it as to the tank: a road is its top speed, open ground half of it, woods a third, no cliff, no water) and shoots UP. One weapon, quad_mg, a MACHINE-GUN mount (ALEX, decision weapon-kinds, 2026-10-11: 'Flak would be shells shot that then explode. Machine guns would be bullets which don't. But Flak is pointed up and machine guns are around and less up. So flak guns have better coverage in the area directly above them.'; on the mapping 'the mobile AA's quad mount and the cutter's guns are machine guns, the cruiser's AA is flak': '5 good'). It was the id aa_guns, shared with the cutter and the cruiser, with the flak's cone (2 degrees to straight up). Now it fires bullets, so it draws TRACERS (data/fx/fx.json tracers.weapons) and its cone is all around and LESS UP: from the horizon to 50 degrees (PROPOSED), so it cannot hit a plane straight over it (a blind disc under the plane) and the flak, which can, has the better coverage there. The reach (600 m effective, 720 m reach), the odds (0.07 a roll), the 2 rolls a second and the 60 deg/s tracking are the former aa_guns' own (PROPOSED, unchanged on purpose: the cone is the only thing that changed). It cannot hurt anything on the ground (its cone starts at the horizon, not below it: a tank is below the muzzle). It carries no bombs and has no specials. THE ART: the drawing layer draws it from a seeded generator with three looks on the board variants/mobile-aa (A half-track with a quad mount, B tracked hull with an open twin turret, C light carrier with a ring mount; nothing is chosen: scripts/ui/unit_marker_art_mobile_aa.gd, data/ui/unit_art_mission2.json). THE NUMBERS' EFFECT, measured by scripts/test_support/mission2_unit_tuning.gd (a plane flying straight over ONE mobile gun, expected pips): see the weapon's base_hit_chance. Record shape: data/units/_schema.json.
name: Mobile anti-aircraft gun

size_m._reason: a light gun carrier is about a tank's length: the unit sheet's tank is 5.6 to 6.6 m, a half-track with a quad mount 6.2 to 6.8, a turreted hull 6.0 to 6.6 and a light carrier 5.8 to 6.4 (data/ui/unit_art_mission2.json); 6.5 is the middle of the three looks. The ground rule checks the hull's two ends at half of it from the centre, so a vehicle this long is kept 3.25 m from a cliff or a shore. NOTE for the scenario's view: the sandbox sizes the planes' drawn scale from the smallest MOBILE unit's size_m (sandbox.gd _ref_size), so a mission with a 6.5 m vehicle and no tank makes this the reference unless that rule asks for the smallest PLANE

draught_m._reason: a ground vehicle does not float: only a sea unit needs water under it (the ground rule keeps it out of water)

actions_per_turn._reason: the tank's two a turn (design doc: 'give each unit type a number of decision points within it, so fast aircraft get several, tanks fewer'): a step is 2.5 s, 22 m on a road at top speed, 45 m a turn

health._reason: a light, thin-skinned carrier: under the tank's 6 and over a light fighter's 3. A bomb's direct hit is 3 pips (data/sim/bombs.json), a near miss 2 or 1, so it goes down to a direct hit and a graze or two near misses; a tank's gun does 1 pip a hit, so four hits. The bomber's guns and the fighters' cones cannot reach the ground at all today, so a bomb is the way a mobile gun is cleared unless the mission adds another

sight_range_m._reason: a gun crew and a commander looking for planes: the tank's 600 m, under the fighters' 800 and the battery's 700, so a fighter sees the gun before the gun sees the fighter; line of sight (data/view/fog.json) cuts it where a ridge or a wood hides the ground

enabled._reason: a gun carrier smokes when hit

source_m._reason: the engine deck, as the tank's (the carrier is about a tank's length, 6.5 m)

source_back_m._reason: the engine deck at the rear of the hull, as the tank's

rise_mps._reason: the smoulder's rate: a damaged ground or sea unit smokes like a ruin or a wreck (data/fx/fx.json ruin R1 and crash A smolder rise_mps 4.0), so its puffs climb into the faster air above and the plume leans downwind (decisions smoke-consistency, wind-with-height). PROPOSED

speed_min_mps._reason: slow reverse, as the tank: a vehicle can reverse once stopped (design doc, Motion and inertia)

speed_cruise_mps._reason: a steady road march, a fifth under top speed (the AI drives at it and a new vehicle starts at it unless a scenario says otherwise): 7 m/s is about 25 km/h

speed_max_mps._reason: about 32 km/h on a road, the lead's brief (about 8 to 10 m/s on roads), a little slower than the tank's 10: a gun carrier is lighter but carries its ammunition. Off the road the ground rule cuts it (data/sim/ground.json speed_factor: open 0.5, woods 0.3 of this)

dive_speed_max_mps._reason: a ground vehicle cannot dive: equal to speed_max_mps

accel_mps2._reason: from a stop to top speed in 6 s, over two steps: a light engine, a little slower to get going than the tank's 2

decel_mps2._reason: from top speed to a stop in 3 s, a step and a half: brakes and the tracks' drag, which also lets the ground rule slow it into woods or onto a shore within a step

reverse_from_stop._reason: design doc, Motion and inertia: ground vehicles reverse only once stopped

turn_rate_curve_dps._reason: pivot steering, one flat point as the tank's (data/units/_schema.json): a tracked or half-tracked vehicle turns at any speed, 25 deg/s, a little slower than the tank's 30, so a step turns it up to 62 degrees and a full circle takes 14 s

turn_bleed_mps2._reason: as the tank: a vehicle loses a little speed in a hard turn (the inside track brakes), 0.8 m/s per second at the full rate

turn_bleed_exponent._reason: as the planes', boats' and the tank's: gentle turns are nearly free, hard turns bite

altitude_bands._reason: it rides the ground: the surface band (data/sim/altitude.json). Bombs reach it

bands_per_step._reason: a ground vehicle never changes band

climb_speed_cost_mps._reason: a ground vehicle never changes band

dive_speed_gain_mps._reason: a ground vehicle never changes band

hardpoints._reason: the mount's muzzles about 2.6 m above the ground, 0.8 m aft of the hull's middle (the three looks put the mount between 0.2 and 1.6 m aft; the middle of them, a difference of under a pixel at the sim's resolution). A plane at 120 m is 117.4 m above them, one at 400 m 397.4 m: more than the weapon's reach, which is the point

mount_deg._reason: the cone is all around (half_across_deg 180), so the mount does not matter; 0 is the hull's front

half_across_deg._reason: all around (Alex, weapon-kinds: machine guns are 'around'): a mount that traverses all the way round, as before. The azimuth is not part of the cone test (combat.gd), the guns fire at anything in their height band whichever way the hull points

elevation_deg._reason: PROPOSED (decision weapon-kinds; Alex: machine guns are 'around and less up'): the middle of a band from the horizon (0 degrees) to 50 degrees up. Was 46, the flak's cone. The lower edge is the HORIZON, not a little below it (the lead's example was -5): the muzzle is 2.6 m up and every surface unit is at 0 m, so a cone that starts below the horizon would let the guns hit tanks and boats from 30 m out, a ground-fire rule nobody has decided (strafing and ground fire are deferred, decision strafe-later); at 0 degrees the quad mount still cannot hurt anything on the ground

half_height_deg._reason: PROPOSED (decision weapon-kinds): from the horizon to 50 degrees up (centre 25, half 25). Was 44 (2 degrees to straight up). A machine gun does not point straight up: a plane right over the mount (a low one is 117 m above the muzzle) is above 50 degrees from any point inside 98 m of the mount on the ground (a medium one, inside 333 m), a blind disc under the plane, which is where flak has the better coverage. 50 is the lead's example number: a dial for the mission's balance, not a decision (Alex, balance-uncalibrated)

effective_range_m._reason: CHANGED 2026-10-11 by Track M2L at the coordinator's brief, from the battery's light flak's 320 m: 'the mobile guns' reach must contest a MEDIUM approach (400 m band), or the bomber simply flies over them' (the units track's own first number, 320 m, reached the low band only). 600 m effective, 720 m reach with the common 20 percent overshoot. By geometry (the muzzle is 2.6 m up, so a low plane is 117 m above it, a medium one 397 m, a high one 997 m): the LOW band is inside the effective range out to 588 m of ground distance and in reach out to 710 m, the MEDIUM band out to 450 m and in reach out to 600 m, and the HIGH band never (997 m is out of the 720 m reach even from straight below). So the low band is still the most dangerous by geometry: a bigger circle at full odds, and a plane in it is nearer. The odds per roll are the weapon's own (base_hit_chance, rolls_per_second), unchanged, so a bomber crossing the reach spends longer inside it: the measured tables in this file's other reasons (and in scripts/test_support/mission2_unit_tuning.gd) were taken at 320 m and are to be re-read. The Strike has no mobile gun, so nothing of it moves. A dial for the mission's balance, not a decision (Alex, balance-uncalibrated)

base_hit_chance._reason: the battery's light flak's per-roll chance and the boat's: 0.07, at 2 rolls a second (half the battery's light guns), so 0.14 hits a second on a plane in range before the other factors. MEASURED (scripts/test_support/mission2_unit_tuning.gd table A: expected pips lost by a plane flying straight at cruise over ONE standing gun, then 150 m, 300 m and 600 m to one side): bomber low 0.98 / 0.90 / 0.43 / 0.00 of its 8 pips, light fighter low 0.81 / 0.75 / 0.35 / 0.00 of its 3; medium and high 0.00 at every offset (out of reach). The battery's light flak alone is about twice that at low (2.0 pips straight over), the whole battery 4.76 for the bomber. Three of these on a bomber's approach take about 3 pips of 8 at low. A dial for the mission's tuning, not a decision (Alex, balance-uncalibrated); 0.07 -> 0.10 would make it 1.4. RE-MEASURED 2026-10-11 for the machine-gun cone (builder AA, tmp/aa/aa_probe.gd, expected pips per pass for a bomber at cruise, straight over / 300 m aside): low 2.03 / 1.85 -> 1.82 / 1.85, medium 1.70 / 1.40 -> 0.61 / 0.92 (the 50-degree cap leaves a medium plane out of the cone inside 333 m of the mount on the ground; the odds themselves are unchanged)

rim_odds_factor._reason: flat, as every flexible gun: a gun crew aims within the arc

falloff_exponent._reason: no effect while the factor is flat (rim_odds_factor 1)

tracking_dps._reason: fast tracking, it is a light gun: the battery's light flak's 60 deg/s and the boat's, three times the heavy flak's 20. A plane right over the guns at low height crosses the line of sight at 40 to 50 deg/s

damage_pips._reason: one pip a hit like every other gun: the light guns hurt by volume, not by weight of shell

rolls_per_second._reason: the patrol boat's twin mount: two rolls a second, half the battery's light flak (4), because it is one mount on a vehicle. The dial with base_hit_chance for how dangerous a hunting gun is
